title: Execution of a register-copy routine
statement: Fix a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ over Boolean symbols and a computation mode, and let $y$ be an input word, $B$ a register bound, $c$ a copy instruction, and $v$ an initial assignment of natural numbers to the $21$ registers. If every register value in $v$ is at most $B$, and the destination register's initial value is at most the source register's initial value, then the specified register program has a guarded execution from the copy instruction and assignment $v$ to its prescribed continuation, with the destination assigned the source's initial value and all other registers unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: A finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols
An assignment $v$ of natural numbers to $21$ registers
Every initial register value is at most $B$
The initial destination value is at most the initial source value
caveat: The claim's Reach predicate depends on a large instruction table and guarded-execution definition; the available definitions do not explain that program informally.
